name: caught_up_survives_compaction_push
comment: review F5-03/PH0-D24: a reader caught up at head=0 right after the first snapshot holds (no timeout_ms); a SECOND snapshot_push (a redundant re-assertion / compaction, same writer) does NOT advance head (PH0-D20: a snapshot consumes no delivery-sequence slot) so the reader's stored cursor is still exactly caught up -- this step emits NOTHING (the hold is untouched, no spurious `reset`); a follow-up probe at the same cursor confirms would_block, not reset
